stem: Mumps virus belongs to which viral group?

options.label: A
options.text: Herpesvirus, grouped with varicella-zoster and herpes simplex viruses
options.misconception: Links mumps with varicella-zoster virus because both are components of the MMRV vaccine.
options.explanation: Herpesviruses such as varicella-zoster and herpes simplex are enveloped DNA viruses; mumps virus is an RNA paramyxovirus.

options.label: B
options.text: Paramyxovirus, grouped with parainfluenza and Newcastle disease viruses
options.misconception: None — mumps is a paramyxovirus related to parainfluenza virus.
options.explanation: CDC classifies mumps virus as a paramyxovirus in the same group as parainfluenza and Newcastle disease viruses, whose antibodies cross-react with mumps.

options.label: C
options.text: Picornavirus, grouped with poliovirus and coxsackieviruses
options.misconception: Groups mumps with the enteroviruses because both can cause aseptic meningitis.
options.explanation: Picornaviruses such as poliovirus and coxsackievirus are small nonenveloped RNA viruses; mumps virus is an enveloped paramyxovirus.

options.label: D
options.text: Orthomyxovirus, grouped with influenza A and B viruses
options.misconception: Confuses orthomyxovirus (influenza) with paramyxovirus because the family names sound alike.
options.explanation: Orthomyxoviruses are the influenza viruses, with segmented genomes; the similar name does not make mumps virus one of them.

options.label: E
options.text: Hepadnavirus, grouped with hepatitis B virus
options.misconception: Associates mumps with hepatitis B because both are viral infections covered by routine vaccines.
options.explanation: Hepadnaviruses such as hepatitis B virus are partially double-stranded DNA viruses that infect the liver, unlike mumps virus.

context: Learning objective: Mumps virus is a paramyxovirus, grouped with parainfluenza and Newcastle disease viruses, whose antibodies cross-react with mumps.
